posts.summary: Conditional strengthening of the Lang–Plaut nonembedding obstruction: a doubling rectifiable curve in Hilbert space with no finite-dimensional bi-Lipschitz embedding. The upstream Hilbert nonembedding theorem is an explicit premise.
posts.body:
**Conditional strengthening: a doubling rectifiable curve with no finite-dimensional bi-Lipschitz embedding.**

The paper [Doubling rectifiable curves with no finite-dimensional bi-Lipschitz embedding](https://mathdb.com/abs/2610.00030) constructs, under its stated source assumption, a Lipschitz image Γ of [0,1] in every infinite-dimensional real Banach space. It is doubling in the restricted ambient norm metric and admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional real normed space at any finite distortion. The same compact, path-connected set has finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure and works for every target dimension and distortion.

Taking the ambient Banach space to be a Hilbert space gives a negative answer to the question on this page, **conditional on the pinned OpenAI Hilbert nonembedding theorem**. The additional contribution is the rectifiable-curve construction preserving the obstruction. This does not independently prove the upstream nonembedding theorem. No injective parametrization or simple arc is claimed.

The full manuscript and supporting package are available on [Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23432132](https://zenodo.org/records/23432132).

**Source and review status.** The upstream inputs are stipulated at [OpenAI/math revision fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb](https://github.com/openai/math/tree/fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb). This is an AI-assisted manuscript with internal project reviews, not external peer review. The supporting Lean checks cover selected lemmas, not the full theorem.

posts.summary: Conditional planar no-bigeodesics extension to every nonatomic edge-weight law on [0,∞), removing the moment assumption. This relies on the stipulated OpenAI source theorem and its operative proof inputs; it is not an independent resolution.
posts.body:
**Conditional solution: removing the moment assumption from a stipulated planar no-bigeodesics theorem.**

The paper [Removing the moment assumption from a stipulated planar no-bigeodesics theorem](https://mathdb.com/abs/2610.00759) deduces that, for every nonatomic Borel probability law G on [0,∞), iid edge weights on the nearest-neighbor square lattice almost surely admit no bigeodesic, simultaneously over all bi-infinite simple paths, without a moment assumption or prescribed direction.

This conclusion is **conditional on source S and its operative proof inputs under their stated hypotheses**, as specified in the manuscript. The stipulated source already covers E[min(X₁,X₂,X₃,X₄)²] < ∞. The extension addresses its infinite-moment complement through the lifted limiting-graph coupling and transferred proof estimates. It relies on the source proof machinery, not merely a black-box finite-moment conclusion.

This matches the two-dimensional problem on this page. It makes no claim in higher dimensions and is not an independent validation of the upstream no-bigeodesics argument. In particular, the upstream family212 selected Lean statements concern limit-shape differentiability, not the absence of bigeodesics; the present package also does not formalize the full probability theorem.

The full manuscript and supporting package are available on [Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23647122](https://zenodo.org/records/23647122).

**Source and review status.** The upstream inputs are stipulated at [OpenAI/math revision fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb](https://github.com/openai/math/tree/fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb). This is an AI-assisted manuscript with internal project reviews, not external peer review. The supporting Lean checks cover selected lemmas, not the full theorem.

posts.summary: Conditional strengthening: two distinct Seymour vertices in every nonempty finite sink-free oriented graph. The paper assumes the one-vertex Seymour theorem and a source pruning lemma, so this is related progress rather than an independent proof of the conjecture.
posts.body:
**Conditional strengthening: two Seymour vertices in every sink-free oriented graph.**

The paper [Two Seymour vertices in every sink-free oriented graph](https://mathdb.com/abs/2610.00028) deduces that every nonempty finite oriented graph without a sink has two distinct vertices v satisfying |N₂(v)| ≥ |N₁(v)|, where N₂ denotes vertices at directed distance exactly two. No extra degree, connectivity, order, or missing-edge restrictions are imposed.

The explicit premises are **the ordinary one-vertex Seymour theorem and the finite-relation pruning lemma stated in the paper from the pinned OpenAI source**. The deduction retains the exceptional boundary after deleting a hypothetical unique good vertex and aggregates gains in a transitive blowup to obtain the second vertex. The two-vertex conclusion is the cited Dara–Francis–Jacob–Narayanan strengthening.

Because the one-vertex assertion asked on this page is itself a premise, this entry is a conditional strengthening and related progress; it is **not an independent proof of Seymour's original conjecture**. The Lean support covers selected finite-cardinality, boundary and pruning consequences, not the full graph argument.

The full manuscript and supporting package are available on [Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23430050](https://zenodo.org/records/23430050).

**Source and review status.** The upstream inputs are stipulated at [OpenAI/math revision fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb](https://github.com/openai/math/tree/fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb). posts.summary: Conditional multiplicity strengthening of Saxl's conjecture: for staircase ρ=(m,…,1), every nontrivial, nonsign constituent has Kronecker multiplicity at least m−1, with equality at (N−1,1). It relies on stronger stipulated source inputs, not just positivity.
posts.body:
**Conditional strengthening: the sharp minimum multiplicity in a staircase tensor square.**

The paper [The sharp minimum multiplicity in a staircase tensor square](https://mathdb.com/abs/2610.00757) studies ordinary complex tensor-square Kronecker coefficients. For m ≥ 2, N=m(m+1)/2 and ρ=(m,m−1,…,1), its conclusion is

$$g(\rho,\rho,\lambda)\ge m-1$$

for every partition λ of N other than the row (N) and column (1ᴺ). Equality holds for λ=(N−1,1), making the uniform floor sharp.

This is a **conditional quantitative strengthening** of the positivity question on this page. It assumes the manuscript's stipulated source cyclic-polytabloid, module-map, quotient and multiplicity-recursion inputs from OpenAI/math; it does not follow here from an independently established black-box positivity theorem. The additional deduction is the uniform quantitative bound through the four-exception invariant, predecessor bounds and low-capacity Kostka estimate.

This entry does not claim an independent proof of the original Saxl conjecture, nor a symmetric-square, exterior-square, integral or modular analogue. The Lean support concerns selected finite-poset and ordered-cut lemmas; the representation theory and full multiplicity theorem remain outside that formalization.

The full manuscript and supporting package are available on [Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23647109](https://zenodo.org/records/23647109).

**Source and review status.** The upstream inputs are stipulated at [OpenAI/math revision fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb](https://github.com/openai/math/tree/fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb).
